extracted.intended_audience: general readers and students of literature, art, and intellectual history
extracted.subtask_description: Extracting evaluative principles and aesthetic/methodological standards implied or stated in a biographical/encyclopaedic treatment of Goethe — i.e., criteria used to judge literature, artistic method, and scientific-aesthetic practice. Useful for applying those principles to creative-writing or literary criticism.

rubrics_metrics.name: Imagination tempered by taste
rubrics_metrics.description: "There is nothing worse than imagination without taste."
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Goethe lauded personal restraint and regarded excess as a disease; imaginative writing should be guided by taste and self-control rather than unbridled excess.

rubrics_metrics.name: Classicism as control; Romanticism as sickness
rubrics_metrics.description: "Classicism was the means of controlling art, and that Romanticism was a sickness."
rubrics_metrics.guidance: A formal aesthetic preference: value control, form, and classical discipline in art; view untamed Romantic excess critically when judging literary quality.

rubrics_metrics.name: Olympian quality: loftiness, serenity, objectivity
rubrics_metrics.description: The epithet "Olympian" refers to loftiness, serenity and objectivity as essential characteristics of the poetic type.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Great poetic style is associated with an elevated, composed, and objective stance rather than agitation or excess; use of these qualities is a positive criterion.

rubrics_metrics.name: Tolerance and non-judgmental observation
rubrics_metrics.description: "Large tolerance... quietly follows the stream of fact and of life without passing moral judgments."
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Valuing a tolerant, observational stance in writing and criticism: follow facts and life calmly and avoid overt moralizing; allow depiction rather than judgment.

rubrics_metrics.name: Versatility of form and tone
rubrics_metrics.description: Goethe's work "could be lushly emotional, and rigorously formal, brief and epigrammatic, and epic."
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Literary excellence includes the ability to range across tones and forms — emotional richness alongside formal discipline, concision alongside epic scope.

rubrics_metrics.name: Moral integrity over nationalist propaganda
rubrics_metrics.description: Goethe "would always decline to write poems arousing nationalist passions... 'How could I write songs of hatred when I felt no hate?'"
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Writers should avoid producing work that deliberately foments hatred or serves as propagandistic nationalism; authenticity of feeling and moral integrity are criteria for acceptable subject / tone.

rubrics_metrics.name: Art–science compatibility and dynamism
rubrics_metrics.description: Goethe "saw 'art and science as compatible disciplines linked by common imaginative processes'" and perceived the universe "as dynamic and in constant flux."
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Valuing interdisciplinary approach: creative work benefits from melding scientific curiosity and artistic imagination; prefer portrayals emphasizing process, change, and dynamism.

rubrics_metrics.name: Experiment as mediator between subject and object
rubrics_metrics.description: Goethe's essay title and methodological stance: "The experiment as mediator between subject and object."
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Methodological guideline for empirical/aesthetic inquiry: use experiment or systematic observation to bridge subjective perception and objective knowledge; applicable to hybrid art–science practices.

rubrics_metrics.name: Systematic empirical observation in aesthetics
rubrics_metrics.description: Goethe was "the first to systematically study the physiological effects of colour" and developed a symmetric colour wheel.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Aesthetic theorizing should be grounded in systematic empirical observation (e.g., careful, repeatable observation of perceptual effects) rather than purely speculative assertions.

rubrics_metrics.name: Analytic/mathematical rigor vs aesthetic approach
rubrics_metrics.description: Goethe's "aesthetic approach failed to meet the standards of analytic and mathematical analysis used ubiquitously in modern Science."
rubrics_metrics.guidance: When making scientific claims or crossing into scientific discourse, aesthetic description alone may be judged insufficient; analytic and mathematical rigor are distinct evaluative standards.

rubrics_metrics.name: Inner content, force, variety and depth
rubrics_metrics.description: Praise that Goethe would be surpassed "but only in the way in which the ancients can be surpassed, in inner content and force, in variety and depth."
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Key literary virtues include strong inner substance, energetic force, formal/imagistic variety, and thematic depth; these are positive criteria for evaluating works.

rubrics_metrics.name: Subject-matter openness (including sexuality)
rubrics_metrics.description: Goethe regarded "human sexuality as a topic worthy of poetic and artistic depiction."
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Legitimizes treating private or taboo subjects (e.g., sexuality) in literary work; openness to such materials is an evaluative stance in favour of artistic honesty and exploration.

rubrics_metrics.name: Critique of pure classification and induction
rubrics_metrics.description: Goethe praised Bacon's experimental advocacy but "was critical of Bacon's inductive method and approach based on pure classification."
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Prefers experimental, holistic, and interpretive methods over mere accumulation/classification of facts; in both science-writing and descriptive literature, avoid reducing phenomena to dry taxonomies.

rubrics_metrics.name: Holistic organismic perspective
rubrics_metrics.description: "We conceive of the individual animal as a small world... Every creature is its own reason to be... [not] the question, What are they for? But rather, where do they come from?"
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Advocates a holistic, organismic viewpoint when depicting living beings or systems: emphasize internal coherence, origin and form, and relational wholeness rather than solely utilitarian function.
